text:
sam-sales: Heads-up — Globex procurement has refused the Export Control paragraph in our MSA, saying their internal vendor policy disallows vendor-side export restrictions. PO signed, but procurement/legal are holding signature. Need quick redline + who signs.

nina-legal: Can you paste the exact clause they want removed? Also confirm whether it's about sanctions, data movement, or subprocessors. cc @kevin-security

sam-sales: They pasted this:

```
Export Control: Customer shall not export, re-export, transfer, or disclose any Redwood technology or data outside the United States or to any person or entity on restricted party lists. Customer will comply with U.S. export control and sanctions laws.
```

sam-sales: Procurement says "remove it entirely or we can't process the PO". They also want HSM in the DPA and a 10ms p95 embedding SLA.

kevin-security: 10ms p95 at their described load/region is unrealistic on hosted. HSM is doable only for Private or Dedicated with CMK. On export: we can replace with neutral compliance language and subprocessors disclosure. Do they require that we accept their local law over US law?

marta-ops: Performance note: their volume = ~3k concurrent embeddings, avg 512 tokens. We can offer 50ms p95 on Hosted and 10ms on Private with dedicated GPUs and HSM. Suggest SLA tiering + credits.

nina-legal: Draft redline approach: (1) Replace the hard US-only line with: "Each party will comply with applicable export and sanctions laws; neither party will knowingly engage with restricted parties." (2) Add subprocessors disclosure and attestation clause (SOC2/ISO where available) (3) HSM addendum opt-in for Private deployment (4) SLA addendum that ties p95 to request size and region and includes credit schedule.

elena-eng: Suggest adding a performance appendix limiting the SLA to requests <=512 tokens and requiring batching hints. Also include fallback model variant for lower-cost/latency when thresholds exceed capacity.

sam-sales: Procurement wants signature routing: CFO + procurement only, no engineering sign-off. They also need PO number on invoices and EDI mapping info. Can legal accept countersignature only?

nina-legal: We can accept procurement+exec countersignature for this account but will require an internal attestation that the customer will not unilaterally change security requirements without an addendum. We'll set Redwood signers as Legal Counsel + VP Finance. DocuSign ok.

finance-bot: Automated check: Net30 approved up to $150k monthly spend. Please include invoice to ap@globex.com and PO header field.

sam-sales: They also asked for subprocessors attestations — SOC2 or ISO27001 for preprocessing partner in Ukraine.

kevin-security: We can provide certificates for certified subprocessors; for any without certs we'll supply a mitigations paragraph and evidence of recent audits.

nina-legal: I'll assemble a redline bundle (MSA w/ neutral export clause, DPA with HSM addendum stub, SLA performance appendix, order-form addendum for PO/EDI). Will route countersign to Globex CFO + Procurement and Redwood Legal + Finance. Target to send by EOD.

sam-sales: Thanks — please flag if we need to propose Private deployment pricing to unblock. :thumbsup:
